Customer (Megan Morrison): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Vusi Molefe): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Customer (Mark Martin): I'm looking at a distribution charge on a property that used zero gas this month.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Hi Mark Martin, Vusi Jacobs here — let me pull that up.
Customer (Mark Martin): Can you actually break down where every line item on this bill comes from?
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Thanks for bearing with us on this. Let me go through the bill with you properly.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Can you give me the account number from your bill, or the service address and the name on the account?
Customer (Mark Martin): Yes, same address as always, and the account's under my name.
Customer (Mark Martin): This isn't the first time — I feel like I'm being charged fees just for having an account.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Which line items are you disputing?
Customer (Mark Martin): The distribution charge and the fixed charge. They're bigger than the gas.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Is the property occupied at the moment?
Customer (Mark Martin): It's vacant while we sell it, so the gas is barely on.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Have you raised this with us before?
Customer (Mark Martin): Once before, and I was told it's just how the bill works.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the itemized charges line by line against metered usage and the current distribution rate schedule.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): The distribution charge and the fixed daily charge are set by the AUC for your rate class, so they apply even when the meter reads zero.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): I've gone through every line — the distribution charge and fixed monthly charge apply regardless of usage under your rate class, and I've corrected the one line item that was billed in error. You'll see the adjustment on your next statement.
Customer (Mark Martin): So one of them was actually wrong?
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Yes, a late-payment charge was applied after your payment had already cleared. That's the adjustment.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): To recap: the late-payment charge comes off on your next statement, and the line-by-line breakdown is in your email.
Customer (Mark Martin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

APX-000805.transcript:
Customer (Brian Baker): I didn't get a bill for eight months, and now you've cut off my gas over it.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Hi Brian Baker, Karabo Zulu here — let me pull that up.
Customer (Brian Baker): How does a bill just not go out for eight months without anyone catching it on your end?
Agent (Karabo Zulu): That's a lot to land on you at once. Let me go through the account history properly.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Can you give me the service address and the name you expected the account to be under?
Customer (Brian Baker): The rental in Leduc, and I assumed gas was in the city utility bill.
Customer (Brian Baker): I don't understand how you can even take a meter reading on an account you told me didn't exist.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Did you receive any letters from us while you lived there?
Customer (Brian Baker): Nothing. Not one bill, not one notice.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Were you paying a utility bill to anyone else in that time?
Customer (Brian Baker): The City of Leduc utility bill. I thought gas was part of it.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Has the service been reconnected yet?
Customer (Brian Baker): It came back on after I called, but only after I'd been told I had no account.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Let me take a look. I've pulled the full account history, confirmed the eight-month billing gap against metered usage, and reviewed how the reconnection was handled.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): The meter kept recording usage the whole time, but the account wasn't set up in your name, so no bill was generated.
Customer (Brian Baker): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): I've confirmed the balance is accurate against metered usage over the unbilled period, but I don't have authority to waive it — what I can offer is a payment plan so the CA$1,800 isn't due all at once.
Customer (Brian Baker): So I still owe all of it?
Agent (Karabo Zulu): The balance matches the metered usage, so yes. It doesn't have to be paid at once, though.
Customer (Brian Baker): Who looks at how this happened?
Agent (Karabo Zulu): I've sent it to the billing team as an account set-up error so it's reviewed, and I'll call you with what they find.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): To recap: the balance stands, a payment plan is available whenever you want it, and the billing team is reviewing how the account was missed.
Customer (Brian Baker): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.
